scenes.text: The TI-84 — the calculator millions of students carry to every exam — just received its most significant hardware upgrade in years.

The Evo packs a three-times faster processor and a fifty percent larger display — three-twenty by two-forty pixels with sixteen-bit color. USB-C replaces the aging port, and a cleaner icon-based interface reduces clutter.

A new Points of Interest Trace feature automatically flags key values while you analyze functions. The updated Lines and Conics app adds equation templates and direct intersection tracing — and a yellow help bar offers contextual guidance without revealing answers.
The Evo is approved for the SAT, ACT, AP, and IB exams. Every retail purchase includes a free four-year online calculator license — an eighty-dollar value bundled in.
